goals: mechanistic: characterize local runoff generation (surface runoff, sub-surface drainage) and snow accumulation/melt across the basin's elevation and soil heterogeneity
validation: reproduce the daily streamflow hydrograph at the American River gauge and report NSE (the stated deliverable)
key_processes: runoff routing and basin aggregation (NOT in stack)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves vertical water/energy balance and snowpack per location, which underlies runoff generation. It cannot route or aggregate runoff to a gauge, so it cannot directly produce a streamflow hydrograph.

feasibility.verdict: partial — the stated deliverable (daily gauge hydrograph + NSE) is NOT achievable with the current stack; only local runoff-generation characterization is
answerable: local water partitioning (ET, surface runoff, drainage) at stratified columns
snowpack accumulation/melt AT each column given its supplied forcing
soil-texture control on local runoff generation under a common forcing

not_answerable.aspect: daily streamflow hydrograph and NSE at the American River gauge
not_answerable.why: ELM is single-column with no channel routing or contributing-area aggregation; a gauge hydrograph is a routed, basin-integrated flux the framework cannot assemble
not_answerable.needs: runoff routing / basin aggregation to gauge cross-section

not_answerable.aspect: elevation control on snow and hydrograph timing (the dominant control in this snowmelt basin)
not_answerable.why: framework lacks elevation-downscaled forcing (T/precip lapse rates, precip-phase); columns at different elevations under uniform forcing would differ only by soil, not climate/snow
no simulated streamflow time series exists to compare; NSE requires routed daily discharge
not_answerable.needs: streamflow output + observed-gauge ingest and NSE computation

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x dominant soil classes)

classes: fine/clay — as sampled from gridded soil raster

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands x 3 dominant soil classes = 9 columns spans the basin's runoff-generation heterogeneity with one representative column per stratum. This resolves the FEASIBLE mechanistic goal; it is deliberately small because with uniform forcing the elevation axis cannot carry a true climate/snow signal (see feasibility) and denser sampling would not change that.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: concentrate columns in the rain-snow transition band, where snowpack sensitivity and thus runoff-timing sensitivity is greatest; place remaining columns to cover the coarse-vs-fine soil contrast that most affects infiltration vs surface runoff.
sampling_strategy.replication: none — single representative column per stratum; replication is not justified until elevation-downscaled forcing makes the elevation axis physically meaningful.

sampling_plan.reason: highest sensitivity of snow accumulation/melt and runoff timing; sampled across three soil classes to isolate infiltration control
characterizes spring-freshet source zone runoff generation across soil classes
characterizes rain-driven runoff/ET partitioning near the valley/gauge across soil classes

validation_design.observation_source: USGS gauge: American River nr Nile (daily)
validation_design.comparison: aggregated — WOULD require routing/area-weighted aggregation of column runoff to the gauge; NOT possible with current stack, so this validation cannot be executed as requested
validation_design.metric: NSE (requested) — cannot be computed without routed simulated streamflow
validation_design.n_validation_points: 1 gauge (daily series) — but no simulated counterpart is producible

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline uniform basin forcing (1980-2018 available), native gridded soil per column

requires_capabilities.capability: runoff routing / basin aggregation to gauge
requires_capabilities.why: convert per-column QOVER+QDRAI into a routed daily discharge at the gauge cross-section
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire streamflow-hydrograph deliverable and NSE

requires_capabilities.why: snowmelt timing in this basin is controlled by elevational precip-phase and SWE distribution
requires_capabilities.blocks: reproducing hydrograph shape/timing; makes the elevation stratification physically meaningful

requires_capabilities.capability: streamflow/discharge output plus observed-gauge ingest and NSE computation
requires_capabilities.why: no comparison time series or metric pipeline currently exists
requires_capabilities.blocks: reporting NSE against the USGS gauge

requires_capabilities.why: soil-moisture and snow states must equilibrate before a defensible 1980-2018 evaluation period
to interpret melt-driven runoff at snow-dominated columns
requires_capabilities.blocks: attributing runoff timing to snow processes

assumptions: Gridded soil raster and DEM are available for the downstream expander to place the 9 stratified columns; I do not supply coordinates or soil values.
Forcing 1980-2018 is basin-uniform (no elevation downscaling) unless a downscaling capability is added.
The USGS gauge provides daily discharge over an overlapping period with the forcing years.
open_questions: Is any runoff-routing or aggregation tool planned? Without it the requested NSE deliverable is unreachable — should the goal be re-scoped to local runoff-generation analysis?
Can elevation-downscaled forcing (lapse rates, PRISM/gridMET-style) be provided? It is essential for hydrograph timing in a snowmelt basin.
What contributing drainage area does the American River gauge integrate, and does it fall within the HUC bbox for aggregation once routing exists?
